PullRequest.Title: agentHost: fix cloud sandbox history replay
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Fix opening existing offline Cloud Sandbox conversations from persisted AHP history.

- Skip identical replication records already processed within the current mirror epoch, so overlapping records do not fail sequence validation or apply text deltas/chunks twice. Preserve rejection of genuine gaps and conflicting records, reset duplicate tracking at mirror restarts, and avoid rewinding the session timestamp.
- Resolve the host-announced default chat, or the sole recorded chat when no default designation was persisted, instead of creating an empty chat at an assumed URI. Keep peer transcripts separate and reject ambiguous multi-chat histories without a recognized default.
- Add regression coverage for duplicate frames/chunks, restarts, conflicts, timestamps, and host-provided chat identities.

The shared replay fix applies to both the editor and Agents window; it does not hide Cloud Sandbox sessions, wake offline environments, or implement missing-frame recovery.

## Validation

- `npm run compile` — passed.
- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/taskEventReplay.test.ts` — passed, 27 checks.
- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/remoteAgentHost/editorCloudSandboxContribution.test.ts --grep 'opens original offline history|opens the original live session|falls back to original history'` — passed, 3 tests.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/taskEventReplay.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/taskEventReplay.test.ts` — passed.
- Replayed the reported session's real history through the production read-only content provider and verified five requests and five responses. Raw history was kept local and removed after validation.
- Launched the current Code OSS build and verified the workbench is responsive; opening the affected conversation through the running UI was not automated.

(Written by Copilot)

Scenarios.Scenario: First open of an offline Cloud Sandbox conversation using prefetched persisted AHP history
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Environment status resolution completes first; for an offline environment, the prefetched Mission Control history request, JSON body read, event decoding/reassembly, reducer folding, and turns-to-history conversion must complete before the transcript renders. The changed duplicate index and equality check run synchronously on this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET the sandbox environment record to decide between live connection and persisted history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per activation attempt for an environment with a task.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same environment-status request and ordering existed before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the offline/history branch is selected.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: GET /agents/tasks/<id>/events and read/parse the complete AHP JSON response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for the opening activation; all events for the task are returned and replayed together.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single full-history request and replay path existed before the diff; the diff adds duplicate recognition inside replay but no additional boundary calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The response, JSON parsing, replay, and history conversion must finish before transcript content is available.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reassemble chunk envelopes, parse completed chunk groups, index sequence records, and fold action envelopes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential pass over E persisted records; Map lookup/set is O(E), and deep equality traverses only D records whose sequence number has already appeared, proportional to the duplicated record bytes. Unique records hit equals(undefined, value) and return immediately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Replay already validated, reassembled, parsed, and folded every record; it did not allocate one Map entry per unique sequence and stopped with an error at the first overlapping record. The added Map is response-scoped and stores references to records already retained by the response array.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous CPU and allocations occur after JSON parsing and before transcript rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The complete persisted event count E, duplicate count D after mirror-batch overlap, action count A, and chunk payload bytes. The changed work is O(E) small Map entries plus O(total bytes of D exact duplicate records), while existing reassembly/folding remains O(E + payload bytes + A).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One environment-status request precedes one history request for this activation. The history promise is passed into the read-only handler and consumed once, preventing a duplicate first-open request; replay itself is single-threaded and sequential.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The in-flight prefetch is reused for the first open and then deliberately cleared. There is no persistent replay cache or negative cache; this diff does not alter those policies. Sequence tracking is per replay and cleared at mirror epoch restarts, then released after folding.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous call path and linear scaling; high confidence that no boundary fan-out, concurrency burst, or lifetime retention was introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very long token-delta histories can contain many records, but the added Map retains only references plus per-entry metadata while the parsed response already owns the full objects. No evidence establishes enough incremental allocation or duplicate comparison to produce user-visible latency or GC pressure.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The new response-scoped linear index is necessary to recognize non-adjacent overlaps, avoids replaying duplicate chunks/deltas, and does not retain history beyond the existing replay lifetime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Later reopen or additional content resolution through the read-only Cloud Sandbox provider
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the one-shot prefetch is consumed, provideChatSessionContent performs a fresh history request, parses and replays the complete response, selects the requested session/default chat, and converts turns before rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the task's complete persisted AHP event history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per later content resolution after the prefetched promise has been consumed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Later opens already fetched and replayed the complete history afresh so stale prefetch data would not pin the transcript.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks that transcript resolution until response parsing and replay finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build a per-epoch sequence index and compare repeated sequence records while decoding the fetched response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One linear index construction per fetched history; deep traversal only for repeated sequence numbers, with the index reset on a mirror restart.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior decoder had no duplicate index and rejected the first overlap instead of producing a transcript.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds transient CPU/allocation before rendering on each later resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Persisted records and duplicate bytes in the task history per reopen; no multiplication by number of chats because one fetched task response is replayed once and sessions/chats are grouped in memory.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each provider resolution awaits its own request; no shared replay cache or coalescer exists after first use. The diff neither adds resolutions nor changes request concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold on each later resolution by design; first-open prefetch is no longer available. No positive or negative replay result persists, and the diff does not modify this lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that later resolutions refetch and replay and that this behavior predates the diff; high confidence that the diff adds no request or concurrency amplification.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency of repeated later content resolutions and maximum production history size are not established. The incremental index is transient and linear, so available code evidence does not support a meaningful regression even though repeated opens repeat it.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Existing repeated full-history reads are outside PR causality, and the changed duplicate handling adds only bounded per-response linear work while enabling successful replay.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced offline first-open and later read-only reopen paths through network fetch, JSON parsing, chunk reassembly, reducer folding, and rendering conversion. Considered repeated work, serialization/allocation, cache lifecycle, boundary fan-out, concurrency, and retention. The change introduces a transient per-epoch sequence Map and duplicate-only deep comparisons, but no extra boundary calls, fan-out, persistent retention, or superlinear work; no actionable performance issue was found.
